region_rules.topic: Leave-takers are protected from the count
region_rules.fact: An employer cannot pad or shrink a layoff with people on paid family or medical leave; they are excluded from the layoff total by statute.

region_rules.topic: The slowest final paycheck in the Northwest
region_rules.fact: Your last wages are due at the end of the pay period, not on your last day. If the period just started, the wait can be two weeks or more.

region_rules.topic: Severance and benefits do not collide
region_rules.fact: The Employment Security Department does not subtract severance from your weekly benefit, so a lump sum and a claim can run side by side.

Until June 29, 2027, a non-compete is void below $126,858.83 a year (2026 figure). Above it, a laid-off worker can be held to one only while the employer keeps paying base salary, less any new earnings. From June 30, 2027, HB 1155 makes employee non-competes void for everyone.
The state age law applies to employers with 8 or more persons, so a release of age claims has value at firms far smaller than the federal 20.
Final wages: due at the end of the pay period in which you were discharged.

region_rules.topic: A promised severance is a wage claim
region_rules.fact: Wisconsin's wage statute names severance provided by agreement or established policy as wages. If the handbook says 2 weeks, you can file for it with the Department of Workforce Development like unpaid pay.
Federal WARN needs 50 job losses; Wisconsin's business-closing law is triggered by 25 employees or 25% of the site, so mid-size cuts are covered here that are not elsewhere.
Severance only counts against a given week if the employer has definitely allocated it to that week and told you so. An unallocated lump sum often does not reduce benefits.
If any part of a non-compete is unreasonable, the whole clause fails. A court cannot shorten it to something fair, which weakens most boilerplate restrictions.

region_rules.topic: Age law with no size floor
region_rules.fact: The Fair Employment Act applies from a single employee and protects workers 40 and up, so an age-claim release has value at even the smallest employer.

region_rules.topic: Payday timing for the last check
region_rules.fact: Final wages are due by the date you would ordinarily have been paid. That is slower than same-day states but has a clear, checkable date.

Business-closing or mass-layoff notice: 60 days before a covered event.
OWBPA (age 40+): 21 days to review a release of age claims, 45 in a group, 7 days to revoke after signing.
Unemployment: file promptly and ask whether your severance has been allocated to specific weeks.
